title: EnerGNN: Learning Optimization-Compatible Energy Functions for Exact Constrained Combinatorial Inference
claim: A three-stage procedure encodes the instance with a graph network, learns a scalar energy over candidates, then solves it exactly under hard constraints.
layout: 3 colored panels, left-to-right, numbered stage titles with a candidate-solutions sketch
description: A wide horizontal figure split into three tinted rounded panels, read left to right: 1. Encode Graph (blue), 2. Learn Energy Landscape (yellow), 3. Solve Exactly (purple). In panel 1, a small bipartite graph with constraint nodes c1, c2 and variable nodes v1–v3 feeds a blue 'Bipartite MPNN' box, which outputs a green column of node embeddings {h_v}. In panel 2, a red binary vector y is combined with the embeddings through a sum node Σ, using the formula z(G,y)=Σ y_v h_v. This passes to an orange 'Energy Head, ReLU MLP' box and then to E_θ(G,y). A small curve beneath marks suboptimal versus near-optimal candidate solutions. In panel 3, a lavender 'MIP encoding' tag leads into a boxed 'Exact MIP Inference' block with argmin E_θ(G,y) s.t. A_y y ≤ b_y, producing a green feasible optimum y*. A badge reads '+ Zero-Shot Constraint Injection'.
caption: EnerGNN encodes an optimization instance using a bipartite message-passing GNN, learns an optimization-compatible energy function over binary configurations, and performs exact constrained inference by globally minimizing the learned energy over the encoded feasible set.
abstract: Learning-based approaches to combinatorial optimization often predict solutions directly or use predictions to restrict search, while expressive energy-based models typically rely on approximate inference. We introduce EnerGNN, a framework that learns energy functions over complete binary configurations and minimizes them under explicit hard constraints through mixed integer programming (MIP). EnerGNN combines a graph neural network encoder with an optimization-compatible readout and a nonlinear energy head, enabling exact constrained inference over the learned energy. An optimality-aware contrastive loss trains the energy to reflect solution quality and constraint violations. Across Quadratic Knapsack, Combinatorial Auctions, and a personalized cell therapy supply chain problem, EnerGNN achieves near-optimal solutions with 100% feasibility. On the supply chain problem, it achieves a 0.05% mean primal gap and a 17.4$\times$ speedup over the monolithic MIP. The learned energy also generalizes to larger instances and supports zero-shot constraint injection, adapting to changing constraints without retraining while preserving feasibility.
